intent: To demonstrate the unequal distribution of vaccine doses globally, highlighting that high-income countries acquired the majority of supplies while lower-income countries received very few.

units.meaning: High-income countries accounted for 54.44% of the relative dose share, i.e. over half (majority).
accepted_routes: High-income countries got 54.4% of doses, more than half.
Over half the doses (54.44%) went to high-income countries.
High income crossed the 50% majority threshold with a 54.44% share.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The High income bar/segment must be visibly labeled 54.44% (or 54.4%) and/or shown crossing a 50% reference line.
units.temporal_anchor: the narration clause that high-income/rich countries held over half / acquired the majority
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly show high income exceeding 50%, or is a general 'majority' label enough?

units.meaning: Lower-income countries received 270,000,000 doses, only a 3.50% relative share.

basis.note: Absolute dose count for lower-income group.

accepted_routes: Lower-income countries received only 3.5% of doses (270 million).
Just 270 million doses went to lower-income countries, a 3.50% share.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The Lower income bar/segment must be labeled 270M and/or 3.5%.
units.temporal_anchor: the narration clause about poor countries didn't / received very few
units.reviewer_question: Is the absolute 270 million count required, or is the 3.5% share sufficient to convey 'very few'?

units.meaning: The dose shares decline in income order: High income 54.44% > Upper middle income 13.61% > Lower middle income 5.33% > Lower income 3.50%.
accepted_routes: Shares rank High 54.44% > Upper-middle 13.61% > Lower-middle 5.33% > Lower-income 3.50%.
Vaccine share falls as income group falls: 54.44%, 13.61%, 5.33%, 3.50%.
High income first with 54.44%, then upper-middle 13.61%, lower-middle 5.33%, lower-income last at 3.50%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Bars/segments must be ordered by income group and show relative-share labels in descending order.
units.temporal_anchor: the overall unequal-distribution clause / rich vs poor summary
units.reviewer_question: Must the animation display the full four-group ranking, or only the high-vs-low contrast?

units.meaning: High-income countries received about 15.6 times as many doses as lower-income countries (4.2 billion vs 270 million).

basis.note: Absolute dose count for high-income group.
Absolute dose count for lower-income group.

accepted_routes: High-income countries got about 15.6 times as many doses as lower-income countries.
For every dose in lower-income countries, high-income countries got roughly 15.6.
The high-to-low dose ratio was 4.2B to 270M, or about 15.6x.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both high-income and lower-income absolute dose values must be visible and a ratio or '15.6x' annotation must connect them.
units.reviewer_question: Should the animation explicitly quantify the 15.6x high-to-low dose gap, or is that optional detail?

units.meaning: High-income share (54.44%) is larger than all other listed income groups combined, which total 22.44%.
accepted_routes: High-income share (54.44%) exceeds the other three listed income groups combined (22.44%).
High income alone is more than twice the combined share of upper-middle, lower-middle, and lower-income groups.
The other three listed groups together have only 22.44%, versus high income's 54.44%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A combined bar/annotation for upper-middle + lower-middle + lower-income (22.44%) must be compared against the high-income bar/segment (54.44%).
units.reviewer_question: Should the video include the high-income-vs-all-other-listed-groups comparison, or avoid it because the table's relative shares do not sum to 100%?

optional_valid: Lower-middle-income group received 411,000,000 doses, a 5.33% share.
High-income absolute value is 4.2 billion doses.
Lower-middle-income absolute value is 411 million doses.
unsupported_to_avoid: 16% of global population, because population data is not in the table.
Causal claims that wealth caused vaccine acquisition.
Claiming the listed relative shares sum to 100%; they sum to 76.88%.
Upper-middle-income absolute dose value, because the table leaves it blank.
Lower-income countries received zero doses; they received 270 million.
Extrapolating beyond the four listed income groups.
notes: The strongest obligatory units are high-income majority share, lower-income low share, and the income-gradient ranking. Optional derived comparisons such as the 15.6x ratio and combined-others comparison are valid only if clearly labeled as derived from table cells.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
